ENGLISH LANGUAGE — TERMLY EXAM #10 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. An orphan is (1 mark)
   A. a brother or a sister
   B. a child whose parents have both died
   C. a woman whose husband has died
   D. a person who looks after children

2. Which pair of words is a minimal pair for /f/ and /v/? (1 mark)
   A. boy, toy
   B. cat, mat
   C. fine, vine
   D. tin, chin

3. What does the abbreviation 'n.' mean in a dictionary entry? (1 mark)
   A. number
   B. noun
   C. name
   D. never

4. Which of these shows how to say a word? (1 mark)
   A. The page number
   B. The cover
   C. The sound guide next to the headword
   D. The index of the atlas

5. Which noun needs the article 'the' because there is only one? (1 mark)
   A. boy
   B. chair
   C. sun
   D. mango

6. What is a surname? (1 mark)
   A. Your first name
   B. Your family name
   C. Your school
   D. Your address

7. 'Practice makes perfect' teaches us that (1 mark)
   A. perfect people never practise
   B. practice is a waste of time
   C. the more we practise, the better we become
   D. we should never try

8. A new idea in a composition begins (1 mark)
   A. in a new paragraph
   B. in the same sentence
   C. with a question mark
   D. in capital letters

9. Which is a linking word that shows something happened at the end? (1 mark)
   A. finally
   B. then
   C. first
   D. next

10. Which pair is a minimal pair for /e/ and /eɪ/? (1 mark)
   A. pin, bin
   B. let, late
   C. ten, den
   D. pat, bat

11. /p/ is a whispered sound. /b/ is (1 mark)
   A. also whispered
   B. silent
   C. a vowel
   D. voiced, with a buzz

12. Which is the best first step before answering a question on a passage? (1 mark)
   A. Close the book
   B. Read the question and find key words
   C. Copy the passage
   D. Write the answer immediately

13. To scan a text means to (1 mark)
   A. copy the text
   B. draw pictures
   C. look quickly for one fact
   D. read every word slowly

14. In 'bandage', the stress is on (1 mark)
   A. the first syllable
   B. neither
   C. the second syllable
   D. both syllables

15. In which direction does the sun set? (1 mark)
   A. North
   B. South
   C. East
   D. West

16. A friendly letter is written to (1 mark)
   A. someone you know well
   B. nobody
   C. the government only
   D. a stranger only

17. Which foods help the body to grow? (1 mark)
   A. Tea only
   B. Beans, eggs, fish and meat
   C. Sugar and salt
   D. Air

18. A balanced diet is a diet that (1 mark)
   A. has only sweets
   B. has the right amounts of all types of food
   C. has only meat
   D. has no water

19. Which material gives you news? (1 mark)
   A. A dictionary
   B. A story book
   C. A map key
   D. A newspaper

20. Independent reading means (1 mark)
   A. reading aloud to the class only
   B. copying sentences
   C. reading on your own without being told what to read
   D. reading only for exams

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Give three questions to ask yourself when you proofread. (3 marks)

22. Give the meaning of four words from the lesson: injury, treatment, painkiller, poison. (4 marks)

23. Write one sentence using 'present' as a noun and one using 'present' as a verb. Show the stress with capital letters. (3 marks)

24. Describe how you would set up a reading club in your class. (4 marks)

25. Describe the steps to fill in a form correctly. (4 marks)

26. Explain what we learn from the story about honesty. (3 marks)

27. List the three main parts of a composition and say what each does. (3 marks)

28. Explain the rule for changing nouns that end in y into plurals. Give two examples. (3 marks)

29. List three things that make handwriting legible. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — TERMLY EXAM #10 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — a child whose parents have both died
   An orphan has lost both parents.

2. C — fine, vine
   Fine and vine differ only in the first sound, /f/ and /v/.

3. B — noun
   The letter n. shows that the word is a noun.

4. C — The sound guide next to the headword
   Dictionaries show pronunciation beside the headword.

5. C — sun
   There is only one sun, so we say the sun.

6. B — Your family name
   The surname is the family name.

7. C — the more we practise, the better we become
   Repeating a skill helps us improve.

8. A — in a new paragraph
   Each paragraph holds one idea.

9. A — finally
   Finally introduces the last event.

10. B — let, late
   Let and late differ in the vowel sound.

11. D — voiced, with a buzz
   The difference between p and b is the voice.

12. B — Read the question and find key words
   Key words tell you what to look for in the text.

13. C — look quickly for one fact
   Scanning is used to find a name, number or word.

14. A — the first syllable
   We say BAN-dage.

15. D — West
   The sun sets in the west.

16. A — someone you know well
   A friendly letter is personal.

17. B — Beans, eggs, fish and meat
   They contain protein.

18. B — has the right amounts of all types of food
   It has energy, body-building and protective foods and water.

19. D — A newspaper
   Newspapers report news.

20. C — reading on your own without being told what to read
   You choose and read for yourself.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: Does every sentence start with a capital letter? Are words spelt correctly? Does my story have a beginning, middle and end?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible question.

22. (4 marks)
   Answer: Injury: harm done to the body. Treatment: care given to a sick person. Painkiller: medicine that reduces pain. Poison: something that can make you very ill or kill you.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: My uncle gave me a PRE-sent. I will pre-SENT the prize to the winner.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sentence and 1 mark for correct stress.

24. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a day, time and place; give members roles; agree on rules such as taking turns; and read silently then share what was read.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four points.

25. (4 marks)
   Answer: Read the whole form and its instructions, get the facts ready, write neatly in the spaces using block letters if asked, fill every space, check the spelling and sign if needed.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four correct steps.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: Honesty means returning what belongs to others. Neema returned the purse and refused a reward, and her mother said honesty is a great treasure.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for the example, 1 mark for the message.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: Introduction: tells who, where and when. Body: tells what happened in order. Conclusion: tells how it ended or how the writer felt.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part with its job.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: If a consonant comes before y, change y to i and add es (baby, babies). If a vowel comes before y, add s (boy, boys).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule and 1 mark for correct examples.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: Letters of the correct size, letters sitting on the line, even gaps between letters and words, correct spelling.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.
